newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says 142 soldiers, 250 rebels killed.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says 142 soldiers, 250 rebels killed.

text.p: The Sri Lankan army carried out mopping-up operations in the northern town of Paranthan on Friday, a day after repelling a big attack by Tamil rebels that killed 142 soldiers and wounded 232, the Defence Ministry said.
The ministry added in a statement that more than 500 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were killed or wounded in the fighting.
Sri Lankan security forces consolidated their position after the rebels temporarily overran parts of the town's defences early on Thursday in the fiercest fighting since last September.
One military official said in Colombo 20 rebel leaders were believed to have been killed in the fighting, but no government confirmation was available.
"Forces are mopping up the last of the resistance," one official said.
The LTTE, who are fighting for a Tamil homeland in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were not immediately available for comment.
But a London-based spokesmen for the rebels on Thursday denied the army claim of 500 rebel casualties.

Rebel transmissions monitored by the army indicated the rebels had recovered 76 bodies of their fighters. Rebels said they had killed more than 100 soldiers, according to other military officials in the area.

LTTE radio transmissions said some artillery guns, armoured cars and tanks had been destroyed by the rebels, who used five separate human-wave attacks and suicide bombers from three directions to overrun defences at Paranthan, a key road junction town 280 km (185 miles) north of Colombo.
Military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said soldiers had destroyed several artillery pieces to prevent them falling into rebel hands, but declined to say how many.

Paranthan, which sits astride the main north-south highway from Colombo to Jaffna and controls the road junction connecting to the rebel-held town of Mullaitivu, is the first military base to be attacked this year by the LTTE.

Security force officials told Reuters the rebels may have planned to cut off government-controlled Paranthan and Kilinochchi, just south of Paranthan, from the army's main bases in the northern Jaffna peninsula, and capture more guns.
"They probably wanted to cut off these two towns from the north, isolate them and hammer them. But they were not successful," one official said.

Government forces, which captured Paranthan from the rebels last July, pushed further into LTTE territory and took control in August of Kilinochchi, the last major town controlled by the rebels. The rebels have vowed to take back both towns.
In July last year, the rebels overran a key army base at Mullaitivu, killing or capturing more than 1,000 men and dealing the military its biggest blow in the war, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
